narrative.overview: MyDietitian is a paid nutrition-coaching service that lives inside LINE. Its surfaces should feel like a trusted guide who already knows you: warm and encouraging when it matters (a streak earned, a goal hit), quietly precise the rest of the time, never clinical and never shouting. Premium quality is carried by space, restraint, and a single confident green — with deliberate delight bursts reserved for moments that earn retention, not decoration. Density is low for customer surfaces (one glanceable focal point per screen on a phone) and earns the right to be denser only in admin, where the owner scans the business.
keyCharacteristics: One vital green carries customer identity and primary action; admin teal is owner-only; everything else is neutral or reserved data color.
Soft 14–18px corners, near-flat surfaces, whisper-light shadows.
Warmth from green, encouraging copy, and roundness — never from a warm-tinted background or chatbot chrome.
Delight bursts (streak pill, goal-hit badge, progress fill) are earned moments — not ambient decoration.
Restraint as the premium signal: space over decoration.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Customer surfaces have exactly one brand green: Vital Green #18B98C. The settings surface's brighter LINE-green (#1db446) on warm paper (#fffdf5) with Kanit is drift to reconcile, not a second accent.

rules.name: The Reserved-Data Rule
rules.body: Amber, coral, violet, and calorie-blue are data colors only — macros, gauges, charts. Forbidden as decoration, button color, or section accent.

rules.name: The Encouragement-Tint Rule
rules.body: Warm tinted fills (#FFF3E0/#9A5B00 for streaks, #E7F7F0/#0E8A67 for progress badges) are allowed only on earned-moment chips and badges — never as page backgrounds or card fields.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes are fixed px, never fluid clamp() on product UI headings. A heading that shrinks inside a panel looks worse, not designed.

rules.name: The Thai-Headroom Rule
rules.body: Never set line-height below 1.3 on Thai headings; test real Thai copy and long member names at 360px before shipping.

rules.name: The Whisper Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest (0 1px 3px / 0.05). A heavier shadow is a response to state (hover, float), never decoration.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter, frosted overlays, and gradient page backgrounds are forbidden on customer surfaces. Depth is tonal, not optical.

rules.name: The Flush-List Rule
rules.body: Repeated records are flush rows divided by hairlines — never a grid of identical cards. The card grid is reserved for a handful of headline stats.

rules.name: The One-Hero Rule
rules.body: Each admin tab and the customer dashboard lead with exactly one focal metric. Secondary numbers demote to a strip or recede in size — never six equal cards competing for attention.

dos: Do keep one vital green (#18B98C) as the only customer identity + primary-action color; admin teal is owner-only.
Do lead each surface with a single glanceable focal point and let the rest recede.
Do use encouragement chips (streak pill, progress badge) as earned delight bursts — warm copy + tinted pill, not more UI chrome.
Do use flush hairline-divided rows for lists; reserve the card grid for a handful of headline stats.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest (0 1px 3px / 0.05); let shadow appear only on hover/float.
Do put :hover, :focus-visible, :active, and :disabled on every interactive element.
Do test real Thai copy and long member names at 360px before shipping.
Do unify settings.html to dashboard tokens (system sans, #18B98C, cool #F4F6F5 field).
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS dashboard — endless identical icon-heading-number cards in a uniform grid.
Don't drift toward clinical / hospital coldness — sterile blue-white, sharp grids, lab-report sterility.
Don't ship cluttered number-walls — dense data with no hierarchy where everything is the same weight.
Don't look like a generic LINE chatbot or food-logging app — bubble UI clichés, neon fitness tropes, calorie-counter aesthetics.
Don't use a warm cream/paper/parchment background; the field is the cool off-white #F4F6F5.
Don't introduce a second customer green (#1db446), Kanit as a second font, or glassmorphism on customer surfaces.
Don't use data colors (amber/coral/violet/blue) as decoration or buttons.
Don't reach for a centered modal when a bottom-sheet drawer or inline expansion will do.
Don't set muted gray (#7A8088) as body text on a tinted fill without checking 4.5:1.
